title: Design and implement the formal Agent-match Web control surface

verification.name: Expo frontend TypeScript contract
verification.command: COREPACK_ENABLE_PROJECT_SPEC=0 corepack pnpm@9.12.0 --dir apps/starcraft-tmg-expo exec tsc --noEmit

verification.name: real-browser formal Agent match control and screenshots

taskBrief: Implement only the presentation and browser-interaction side of Ticket 23 Slice 248's formal Agent-vs-Agent match control. First study the current Match page, authoritative battlefield workspace, hosted-opponent panel, current StarCraft UI language, responsive layouts and existing browser verifiers; then freeze your own numbered UX plan in the allowed report before implementation. Codex owns and will keep the backend contract unchanged: GET /__ticket23/a2a/ui-status returns {ok, job, manifest}; POST /__ticket23/a2a/ui-drive queues exactly one authoritative Agent action; both use same-origin credentials and are available only to the local formal-evidence server. manifest exposes room.stateRevision, state round/phase/activeSideKey/terminal/gameOver, usage providerCalls/totalUnits/estimatedCostCnyMicros, dataWiringAudit status/schema/hash/blockingFindingCount, recentAcceptedTransitions and the already existing model/Skill evidence. Do not alter, emulate or recalculate Rules, data wiring, probability, legality, Agent strategy, Provider work, credentials, Room state or server endpoints. Design the interaction yourself for a tabletop player: it should feel like a compact StarCraft command surface integrated with the battle table, keep the board as the visual focus, clearly separate preflight/data-gate state from Agent thinking/running/applied/failed states, show round/phase/active side, model/cost usage and the last accepted action, and make the next action understandable before the user starts it. Normal product servers returning 403/404 must hide the experimental control without an alarming product error. A data-gate blocker must visibly prevent execution. The stable action control testID must be agent-agent-drive-next, and the root testID must be agent-agent-match-control. Each user activation must send one and only one POST, remain disabled while queued/running, poll GET status without duplicate submission, recover visibly from a typed failure, refresh the accepted action and room revision, and never expose a cookie/token or raw model content. Desktop Web should use an unobtrusive command strip or dock near the board; narrow/touch App Web should use a compact control that expands without covering required battlefield interaction. Respect reduced motion, keyboard, screen-reader and touch use. Build a focused real-browser verifier with same-origin mocked endpoint responses that proves hidden-on-normal-server, passed/blocked/running/failed/completed states, exactly-one POST, no duplicate click while busy, responsive layout and stable test IDs. Capture desktop and 390px screenshots and write a claim-to-pixel explanation. Run only the two declared gates once after final relevant changes, make scoped commits, do not push, and do not touch existing backend files.
